newsitem.title: UK: Repsol makes new gas find in Egypt's Khalda field.
newsitem.headline: Repsol makes new gas find in Egypt's Khalda field.

text.p: Spanish petrochemical group Repsol said on Thursday it had made a new gas and condensate find in Egypt's Khalda concession.
No figure was given for the discovery's size but Repsol said in a statement that four production tests from one well produced the equivalent of 20,000 barrels a day of oil.
Repsol said the Khalda group planned a further 12 development and 10 exploration wells this year, along with three gas appraisal wells.
Repsol has a 50 percent stake in the Khalda group, the joint developer of the field in northwestern Egypt, along with the Apache Group (40 percent) and South Korea's Samsung (10 percent).

The Khalda group signed a 10-year deal with state-owned Egyptian General Petroleum Co in January to provide 200 million cubic feet of gas per day, mainly for use in power generation for projects in the Alexandria region.

"The signing of this contract implies the development of gas reserves estimated at 14 billion cubic metres and assumes an investment of more than $400 million for the Khalda group," Repsol said in a statement in January.
Repsol said it made six new discoveries last year in Egypt, where it is the third largest oil company behind Amoco Corp and Italy's Agip SpA.
